summary: Local video recorder for IP cameras that uses AI object detection in real time, built to work with Home Assistant.

heroCommands.command: Follow the installation guide at docs.frigate.video

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Frigate is a complete, local NVR (network video recorder) designed for Home Assistant, with AI object detection. It uses OpenCV and TensorFlow to detect objects in real time on your own hardware for IP cameras.
sixtySeconds.problem: Cloud camera services send your footage elsewhere and flood you with motion alerts. Frigate runs locally and only alerts on real objects like people or cars.
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for efficient local detection that only runs where and when motion happens, and tight Home Assistant integration.
requirements: A GPU or AI accelerator is highly recommended

overview: Frigate uses very low-overhead motion detection to decide where to run object detection, and leans on multiprocessing, favouring real time over processing every frame.
It integrates with Home Assistant through a custom component. AI accelerators outperform even the best CPUs with little overhead; see the docs for supported detectors.
Installation and configuration are documented at docs.frigate.video. Frigate is MIT licensed.
limitations: Install steps live in the docs
Works best with an AI accelerator
Respect local laws when recording others
